fichas.title: Fire-resistant glazing: G-glazing
fichas.summary: G-glazing is transparent fire-resistant glazing that can prevent the spread of fire and smoke for its classified duration, but does not prevent transmission of thermal radiation. It may be used where regulations do not require a higher level of fire protection, including lighting openings in fire-retarding corridor walls and some high-rise façades. The lower edge of glazing in corridor walls must be at least 1.80 m above floor level. Glass-brick systems and their installation details are illustrated.
uses: Provide lighting in fire-retarding corridor walls
Limit the spread of fire and smoke for the classified duration
Use in façades divided into horizontal fire compartments

fichas.title: Fire-resistant glazing: F-glazing
fichas.summary: F-glazing is transparent fire-resistant glazing that prevents the spread of fire and smoke and transmission of thermal radiation for its classified duration. It must provide thermal isolation and structural safety; during a fire, the units become opaque and behave like walls for fire-protection purposes. Construction types include pre-stressed double-glazed panes with water-containing gel and multi-pane units with inorganic interlayers. Units are installed in approved systems, including dry-wall partitions, masonry and reinforced concrete. F-glazing is used mainly indoors, with special constructions also available for outdoor use.
uses: Prevent the spread of fire and smoke
furniture_equipment: Inorganic interlayers such as sodium silicate
